It is Natasha "Viper" Kozlov's personal ride when she works alone and the crew's primary "runner" for urgent hand-offs. When an extraction team needs to split the haul, a single rider can peel away on the Blackbird with a backpack full of diamonds while every patrol car chases the van. Its helmet carries a heads-up display linked to the Savant Glasses, showing police positions, traffic signals and Archie's route in real time. By the time a cruiser spots it, the Blackbird is already three intersections away.

name: Bandit
paras: Bandit is a nine-year-old beagle with a gray muzzle, floppy ears and the most dangerous nose in the city. Before joining the crew, he spent seven years as a customs detection dog at the international airport, sniffing out smuggled cash and contraband. He was retired after failing an evaluation — one that Riley "Ghost" Thompson later discovered had been rigged by a corrupt customs officer who wanted Bandit gone. Riley adopted him the same week.

Bandit's specialty is scent. He can follow a single person through a packed subway station, tell which safe-deposit box holds cash or find the one guard in a building wearing a particular cologne. Unlike Echo or Diesel, he isn't tactical, armored or intimidating — he is simply adorable, and nobody suspects a beagle sniffing around a bank lobby. He often joins Sophia and the Puppy on social infiltration jobs, cast as an elderly family pet.

At the safehouse, Bandit sleeps on Riley's server racks for the warmth and steals food from Leon's kitchen with astonishing regularity. He has never once been caught. He was, after all, trained by professionals.

name: Grappling Gun
paras: The Grappling Gun is Isabella "Phantom" Cross's favorite piece of equipment and the reason she can climb buildings faster than most people climb stairs. The compact, pistol-shaped launcher fires a titanium hook trailing a high-tensile microfiber line rated for over 300 kilograms, and a motorized winch in the grip can haul a person up ten stories in seconds or lower them silently into an atrium.

Diego designed the hook with both magnetic and expanding-claw modes, so it bites into concrete, steel beams and skylight frames alike, and the line is coated to be nearly invisible at night. The crew uses it for vertical entries, rooftop escapes and the occasional leap between buildings, with Isabella and Tomi locked in a running contest for the fastest time. There is one rule: the gun is always fired by the person who will ride the line. Bulldozer learned why after a misfire left him dangling from a parking garage for forty minutes while Tomi filmed the whole thing.

name: Dart Pistol
paras: Not every guard needs to be hurt; most just need to be asleep. The Dart Pistol is a compressed-gas tranquilizer gun originally built for wildlife veterinarians, loaded with darts of a fast-acting sedative brewed by Leon "Chemist" Duval. A single dart puts a grown man down within ten seconds and keeps him under for an hour, with nothing worse than a headache when he wakes.

The crew relies on it for the "quiet" phase of an operation, when the specialists must slip past guards without leaving bodies behind. It's also used on guard dogs, a fact Diesel appears to resent personally. Its range is short and the darts are slow, so the shooter must be close and calm. Natasha prefers it to the Whisper whenever she can, and Arthur McGrath called it a toy — right up until he watched it drop a 250-pound security chief mid-sentence.

name: Flashbang
paras: When a plan goes "Loud," the Flashbang is how the crew takes a room in under a second. The stun grenade detonates with a blinding flash and a deafening bang that leaves everyone nearby blind, deaf and disoriented for several seconds — long enough for Bulldozer and Diesel to clear the room without a shot fired.

The crew's flashbangs are custom-built by Diego and Leon, with reduced fragmentation, extra magnesium and delayed fuses so they can be rolled under doors or dropped through vents. Every crew member wears tinted, noise-canceling earpieces that blunt the effect for friendlies, and Diesel, conditioned by the Colonel, doesn't even flinch. The Flashbang is the Protocol in its purest form: control the chaos, own the room, minimize casualties. When the pin comes out, everyone knows the drill — close your eyes, count two, move.

name: Lookout
paras: Every operation needs eyes on every corner, and not all of them can belong to specialists. Lookouts are low-level street hires — teenagers, bike couriers, hot-dog vendors and bored doormen — paid in cash to watch a street and report anything unusual. They don't know who they work for, they don't know what the job is and they never meet the crew. All they know is that if a police car turns onto their block, they send a single text to a burner number. Archie's network includes dozens of them, recruited and paid through Frank "Smiles" Castellano. On the day of a heist, they form an invisible early-warning perimeter around the target — a human tripwire no police scanner can detect. Expendable, replaceable and absolutely essential, they are the street-level nervous system of the entire organization.

name: Crows
paras: Archie taught the crew to trust pigeons. Zara "Freq" Harris taught them to trust crows. Crows are among the smartest animals in the city: they recognize individual human faces, solve multi-step puzzles and hold grudges for years. Zara spent a year training a small murder of them on the safehouse roof, rewarding them with peanuts for retrieving anything shiny.

Now the Crows are the crew's strangest asset. They can snatch a keycard left on a café table, drop a tiny tracker onto the roof of a target's car or stage a sudden, raucous disturbance in a courtyard to pull guards away from their posts. Above all, they are ignored — no security system ever flags a bird. They have names (Edgar, Poe, Lenore and Nevermore) and they bring Zara gifts of bottle caps and lost earrings. They also refuse to go anywhere near Butcher, though they have been seen dropping pebbles on his head from a safe height.

name: Wheelman
paras: Carlos "Rain" Ruiz can't drive every car at once, so the crew draws on a rotating pool of hired Wheelmen — freelance drivers recruited from street-racing circuits, unlicensed taxi services and the occasional disgraced rally team. They are paid per job, told only where to be and when, and expected to keep their mouths shut. A Wheelman might drive a decoy car in the opposite direction, park a Citycar across an intersection or wait in a parking garage with the engine running. Carlos vets every one personally on a closed course where the traffic cones are replaced by Bulldozer standing perfectly still. Only the best get called back. The rest learn quickly that in Archie's world, being late is worse than being caught.

name: Crowbar
paras: Before lockpick guns, RFID cloners and thermal lances, there was the crowbar. A heavy, hooked bar of forged steel, it is the oldest burglary tool in the world and still one of the most effective. It pops windows, pries doors, levers up manhole covers and, in a pinch, ends an argument. Every vehicle in the crew's fleet carries one tucked under a seat. Arthur McGrath claims he opened his first safe with a crowbar at sixteen and won't go on a job without one; Tomi painted his bright red, and Bulldozer's is bent from a story nobody tells. Cheap, silent, untraceable and impossible to hack, it reminds the crew that the simplest solution is often the best one.

name: Ice Cream Truck
paras: Nobody suspects the ice cream truck. Painted in cheerful pastels with a cartoon cone on the side and a looping jingle playing from its speaker, it is the crew's most disarming surveillance and distraction vehicle. It can sit beside a bank, a jewelry store or even a police station all afternoon, and the only attention it draws is from children. Frank "Smiles" Castellano runs it personally, wearing a paper hat and handing out free cones while Maya "Spider" Patel films the target from behind the freezer.

Its real value arrives in the final minutes of a heist. When the jingle switches to a particular tune, it's a signal to the crew outside. And when the truck "breaks down" in the middle of a key intersection, mobbed by kids and parents, the police have no choice but to go around. The freezers are real, the ice cream is real, and the hidden compartment beneath the floor holds exactly one bag of bearer bonds.

name: Brass Knuckles
paras: Brass Knuckles are the last-resort weapon of the crew's street muscle: four rings of solid brass that turn a punch into a hammer blow. They fit in a pocket, pass for a paperweight and need no ammunition, license or training. Thugs carry them for bar fights and back-alley encounters, Bulldozer keeps a pair on his keychain "for decoration," and Frank "Smiles" Castellano owns a gold-plated set he swears he has never used — though he keeps them suspiciously well polished. Crude, simple and brutally effective, they remind everyone in the room that the crew came from the streets, and can always go back there.

name: Tow Truck
paras: A tow truck can drive away with a car in broad daylight, in front of witnesses, and nobody calls the police. The crew's Tow Truck is a battered flatbed with a faded "Rossi's Recovery" logo, operated by a pair of Thugs in grease-stained coveralls. It clears cars blocking escape routes, "recovers" police cruisers parked in inconvenient places and hauls away getaway vehicles before the forensics team arrives. On one legendary job, it towed an armored cash van straight out of a depot lot with the cash still inside. To the city, it's just another tow truck. To Archie, it's a way to make evidence disappear in plain sight.

name: Burner Phone
paras: A cheap prepaid flip phone, bought with cash at a corner store, used for one job and then destroyed. The burner phone is the foundation of the crew's communication discipline. Every member receives a fresh set before each operation, programmed by Riley with numbers known only to the team. When the job is done, the phones are smashed, the SIM cards snapped and the pieces scattered across three different storm drains. Arthur's rules are absolute: never carry a burner for more than 72 hours, and never, ever call home on one. Tomi keeps a box of them under his bed — new, cheap and anonymous, the perfect tool for staying invisible.

name: Mule
paras: Mules are the crew's couriers: low-level hires who carry the goods once the job is done. They don't know where the cash came from or where it's going; they only know they have a duffel bag, a destination and a deadline. The haul moves across the city in stages, handed from one mule to the next on buses, subways and bicycles, so that no single person ever holds it for long. Sam "Cleaner" Lau designed the relay to shatter any trail the police might follow. Most mules are college students and gig workers chasing easy money. They're told the bag contains "legal documents." The smart ones never look inside.

name: Pickpocket
paras: Before Tomi O'Brien became a master thief, he was a pickpocket — and there are a hundred more like him working the city's streets. The crew hires local pickpockets as contractors, sending them into crowded subway cars, bus terminals and shopping streets to lift wallets, phones and keycards from specific targets. A bump, an apology, a smile, and they're gone. Most are teenagers who learned the trade from older siblings. Tomi personally recruits the best, teaching them his tricks and paying them more than any fence would. For most, it's just a quick payday. For a lucky few, it's the first step into Archie's world.
